# dsh-graft-plugin
English | 中文
A DeepSeek Harness plugin that puts graft — a prebuilt graph of every symbol, its `file:line` span,
and who calls what — in front of both you and the model.
It does four things:
- **A chip in the composer** naming the graft index the current session is actually serving, whether
it still matches the code, and how many tokens graft has saved in that repo. Its card carries a **B

uild** button — rebuild the index, or create the first one.
- **Five tools for the model** — `graft_
ask`, `graft_grep`, `graft_callers`, `graft_skeleton`, `graft_map` — resolved per session, so one ds

h can serve several workspaces at once, git worktrees included, each with its own graph.
- **`/graft

`** to build or rebuild the index, and **auto-rebuild** after the model edits files.
- **A `graft vi
z` button** that opens the graph in dsh's built-in right sidebar (0.1.5+), in dsh-better-sidebar if
you still run it, and in a browser tab as the last resort.

e plugin's bundle row whenever the install exits non-zero — the dependency lands, the plugin stays i
nvisible, and dsh starts up cleanly with no error to search for. If `add` ends with `ERR_PNPM_IGNORE
D_BUILDS`, approve and re-run it:

the profile's `package.json`:

ck. If your global npm prefix needs elevation, the postinstall says so and prints the one command to

### In the desktop app
The desktop dsh installs plugins from its own **Plugins** settings — no CLI, no profile directory:

1. Open **Plugins** (settings, left sidebar) and click **Add plugin**.
2. Paste the GitHub repositor
y address into the field (the package name `dsh-graft-plugin` works too):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
3. Click **Install**.
The dialog switches to the **Installed** confirmation, and the plugin appears under **Installed** at
the bottom of the settings page:
> The dialog notes that installed plugins **do not update automatically yet** — to upgrade, uninstal
l and install again. The graft CLI requirement (`npm install -g @nanonets/graft`) is the same.
### The sidebar tab
On dsh `0.1.5` and later the button opens the graph in **dsh's own right sidebar** — a tab titled Gr
aft, also listed on the sidebar's guide page as "The graft graph for this workspace" — and a second
click focuses the tab that is already open. No install needed for that path: the registration is sof
t, so an older dsh without the right sidebar falls through to `dsh-better-sidebar` when it is mounte
d, and to a browser tab when neither is there.
If your profile still runs `dsh-better-sidebar`, that path is tried **first** and behaves exactly as
before. From 0.3.0 it is an **optional peer dependency** — dsh no longer downloads it for you, so a
dd it yourself when you want it (on dsh `0.1.5-rc.2` or later it cannot mount anyway, so most profil
es should skip this):
[代码示例省略，未执行]
> **Compatibility.** `dsh-better-sidebar` 0.18.x requires `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives`, w
hich dsh removed in `0.1.5-rc.2`. On that version or later it will not mount — which is exactly the
profiles where the built-in right sidebar takes over instead. Everything else in this plugin — chip,
tools, `/graft`, auto-rebuild — is unaffected.
The chip, the tools, `/graft` and the auto-rebuild all work without any sidebar; the button simply f
alls back to a browser tab when neither one is present.
> This plugin does **not** insert a `dsh-better-sidebar` row itself, on purpose. That package's own
bundle row carries a guard that disables it when another enabled row already mounts the same package
. A second row with a different id makes that guard circular, and the losing outcome is *your existi
ng sidebar silently disabling itself*. One explicit command is worth more than that risk.
## What you get
### The chip
Sits in the composer next to the model name:

ning saved-token tally, and the `graft viz` button.

`0.2.0-rc.2` | needs plugin `0.2.1`+ — earlier releases fail to activate (see Troubleshooting) |

- Node 22+
- the `graft` CLI on PATH (`npm install -g @nanonets/graft`). A bun global install (`bun
add -g @nanonets/graft`) is detected too, via `$BUN_INSTALL` or `~/.bun`.
The client bundle requires only `react`, which is why it survives the dsh `0.1.5-rc.2` client-packag
e removals that broke several neighbouring plugins.
